data.title: When does the city slow down?
data.headline: Traffic is 52% slower at 9 am than at 5 am
data.detail: Taxis average 10.9 mph at their slowest hour versus 23.0 mph at their fastest, for the same street network. Because the meter charges for waiting time, congestion directly raises the price of a mile.
data.value_label: speed lost at the worst hour

data.title: Who pays most per mile?
data.headline: Under 1 mi trips cost 2.9× more per mile than 20+ mi trips
data.detail: $8.04/mi versus $2.76/mi. The flag-drop and time-based charges dominate short rides, and 27% of trips fall in the shortest band — most riders pay the premium price.

data.title: How much do the airports matter?
data.headline: Airport pickups are 4.9% of trips but 15.5% of revenue
data.detail: Each JFK, LaGuardia or Newark pickup earns about 3.2× an average ride. Counting drop-offs too, 6.4% of all trips touch an airport. Card tips on airport pickups average 21.5% versus 21.7% elsewhere.
data.value_label: revenue per airport pickup vs. average
